02 / DIGITAL-FIRST DISTRIBUTION

A few permanent signs.
A fresh guide every day.

Use one stable web address. Update the dated content at that address.

SCAN TO PREVIEW THE CURRENT GUIDE

Open the guide previewWorking prototype · sample programme
01

Place it where guests pause.

Entrances, Ticket Office, Food Court, restaurant and Arcade.

02

Make opening it simple.

Scan with a phone camera and open the guide in a browser. No app installation is required.

03

Keep the choice clear.

Recommend large mobile buttons: What’s on · Food & offers · Park map. Offer the book view as another way to browse.

Durable QR signs replace the need for a daily handout for every guest. Sign production, maintenance and staff time still have a cost.

03 / REACH & ACCESS

Before arrival.
Throughout the visit.

SOCIAL MEDIA

Bring the day into their feed.

Facebook: daily highlights and a clickable guide link.

Instagram: a Story link sticker and profile link.

TikTok: a short highlights video and profile link, where the account supports it.

PARK COMMUNICATION

Make the guide easy to find.

Add the link to booking and group-visit messages.

If guest Wi-Fi is available, add it to the welcome page.

Show upcoming activities and the QR on park screens.

A HUMAN WELCOME

Let staff introduce it.

“Welcome to BOSCO! Scan here for today’s activities, map and special offers.”

For guests without internet access, staff devices and park screens can show the main information.

On the same phone, use a clickable link.

QR codes work well on signs, printed materials, larger screens or another device.

07 / A CLEAR PROMOTION

Make the offer clear.
Make it easy to claim.

PROPOSED FOOD TRUCK OFFER

Your second
smash burger,
half price.

Buy 2 eligible smash burgers and 1 Pepsi in one order. The lower-priced burger is 50% off.

SHOW CODE: BOSCOBURGER
12–5 PM · Participating Food Trucks · One discount per qualifying bundle. While stocks last. No combined offers. Eligible burgers, Pepsi size and selling prices to be confirmed.

Five answers every offer needs.

  1. What does the guest receive?
  2. How much does it cost?
  3. Where can it be claimed?
  4. When is it available?
  5. How does the guest redeem it?

Agree the cashier process, eligible items and terms before launch. The code above is an example manual redemption method.

Cost the offer before approving it.

09 / DAILY OWNERSHIP & COST

One daily owner.
One coordinated edition.

01

Prepare.

CONFIRM ONE NAMED CONTENT OWNER
02

Confirm.

BRIEF CASHIERS ON ANY PROMOTION

CHECK LINKS AND REMOVE EXPIRED OFFERS

10 / A SMALL, MEASURABLE START

Seven days.
Learn before expanding.

2 QR locations: entrance + Food Court1 participating food outlet1 daily content owner
REACH

Guide visits.

Use agreed link analytics if enabled. Configure measurement before the pilot.

ACTION

Offer redemptions.

Cashiers record the approved offer code and qualifying transactions.

VALUE

Spend & contribution.

Review basket value and profit after food costs and discounts, using comparable trading periods.

EXPERIENCE

Guest & team feedback.

Record useful questions, confusing wording and the staff effort needed each day.

Set the baseline and success criteria before launch. These are measurement proposals, not results; the current guide has no analytics or live redemption tracking.
